blocks.text: Houses for Sale in South Surrey, BC

parts.t: Browse detached houses on regular South Surrey lots at every price, with acreage, farms and mobile homes left out for easy comparison.
These are detached houses for sale in South Surrey: one house on its own lot, at any price. Acreage, farms and mobile homes are left out so you can compare houses on regular city lots.

blocks.text: What kind of lots you'll find

parts.t: South Surrey's house lots vary more than most buyers expect. Part of the reason is history. The City notes in its
zoning summary

that Surrey was first laid out with curved roads and cul-de-sacs, then switched to a straight grid in the 1980s. So many older streets have pie-shaped lots with no lane, while newer areas follow the grid.
The zoning tells you a lot about the lot. On July 8, 2024 the City replaced its old single-family zones with new ones, listed on its
Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing page
R1 Suburban Residential
replaced the half-acre zone.
R2 Quarter Acre Residential
replaced the quarter-acre zone.
R2-O Oceanfront Residential
replaced the oceanfront zone.
R3 Urban Residential
replaced the standard RF zone.
R4 Small Lot
and
R5 Compact
replaced the narrow-lot zones like RF-12 and RF-9.
When you see a listing, ask for the zone. An R2 lot on a quiet older street and an R4 lot in a new subdivision are very different houses, even at a similar price.

blocks.text: South Surrey neighbourhoods for detached houses

parts.t: Crescent Beach is a good example of an older house area. The City's
Crescent Beach Land Use Plan

describes it as a small, mostly residential neighbourhood at the mouth of the Nicomekl River, with Blackie Spit Park and views of Boundary Bay. The plan's goal is to keep its seaside village feel, so don't expect big new subdivisions there.
In the newer Grandview Heights plans, the City set aside low-density land for detached houses and duplexes at 6 to 10 units per acre, per the
Morgan Heights plan

blocks.text: The new housing rules and your lot

parts.t: Because of the B.C. small-scale housing law, Surrey's new zones apply to urban lots under 4,050 square metres (one acre) inside Metro Vancouver's urban containment boundary. The City says that's more than 72,000 lots across Surrey. On those lots, the zones allow combinations like a house with a garden suite or coach house, or a duplex.

Triplexes and fourplexes are allowed in the R3 zone, but the City's summary says they need lane access. With all the older cul-de-sac lots in South Surrey, that rules a lot of lots out. If you're buying a house partly for what you could build later, we check the zone, the lane and the lot shape before you write an offer. The City also started a review of these rules in July 2026, so I'll confirm the current version for any lot you like.

A coach house is a second, smaller home on a house lot. Surrey's small-scale housing page defines it as a dwelling unit above or attached to a detached garage. Most South Surrey examples sit on compact, lane-access lots, which are now zoned R4 or R5. The City's table shows the old RF-12C and RF-9C coach house zones became R4 Small Lot Residential and R5 Compact Residential.
In the R4 zone, Part 16 of Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 sets these limits:
A coach house must be between 35 and 75 square metres, not counting the garage or carport.
Its floor area is allowed on top of the floor area ratio for the main house or duplex.
A coach house is only permitted on lots with lane access, and never in the front yard.
It must be at least 5.0 metres from the main house, and its rear setback can drop to 1.0 metre when it sits above a garage or carport.
It may not exceed two levels.
On a corner lot with a rear lane, the driveway to the extra parking space must come from the lane.

The R5 zone is meant for compact lots, typically with rear lane access, of 291 square metres or more. Surrey's suite page says a secondary suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite. The City also says the 2024 rules don't legalise coach houses built without permits, so ask for the permit and final inspection.

blocks.text: Before you buy a house here

parts.t: Get the title and look for covenants, easements or building schemes, which are common in subdivisions.
Check permits for any additions, decks or finished basements.
On older homes, ask about the roof, the drain tile and the furnace age.
Near the water or a ravine, ask the City about any development permit area that covers the lot.

What zone is a typical South Surrey house lot?

Since July 8, 2024, the old standard RF zone is R3 Urban Residential. The old half-acre and quarter-acre zones are now R1 and R2, oceanfront lots are R2-O, and narrow-lot zones became R4 or R5. Ask for the zone of any house you like.
Can I build a fourplex on a South Surrey lot?
Fourplexes are allowed in the R3 zone, but the City requires lane access for them. Many older cul-de-sac lots don't have a lane, so check the lot first.
Does this page include acreage or farms?
No. It shows detached houses on regular lots. Acreage and farm properties are on their own pages.
What's the detached benchmark price in South Surrey?
FVREB publishes a monthly detached benchmark for South Surrey and White Rock.

Which South Surrey zones allow a coach house?

Surrey's former RF-12C and RF-9C coach house zones became R4 Small Lot Residential and R5 Compact Residential on July 8, 2024. In R4, a coach house needs lane access and must be 35 to 75 square metres, not counting the garage.
Can a coach house have its own suite?
No. The City of Surrey says a secondary suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite.
